correctness.rationale: Reading Eq. (25) with f(y)=-lambda*y and multiplying by D=(3-kappa)(1+kappa) gives exactly the stated B and C. For q=1/(1+z), expansion gives p(q)>0 and 2q>B, so q is strictly above the largest real root whenever real roots exist. For kappa<=1/2 the discriminant is nonnegative through z_c=(1+kappa)/(2(1-kappa)) and B>=0 there. When C<=0 the nonnegative recurrence coefficients suffice; otherwise the two nonnegative roots and the start above the larger one give nonnegative iterates (including the repeated-root solution). Beyond z_c the complex-root sinusoid must have a negative iterate: it either samples a negative arc densely or sums to zero on a nontrivial finite rotation orbit with positive initial value. For kappa>1/2, z_a=(1-kappa^2)/kappa is the B=0 point with C<0 there and below. Beyond z_a, C>=0 gives y_2<0, whereas C<0 gives a larger-modulus negative root with strictly negative coefficient because q exceeds the positive root, forcing eventual negativity on even indices. This verifies inclusivity and the degenerate B=C=0 endpoint, and the strict branch monotonicities give the unique optimum. An independent rational replay gives first negative n=97 at kappa=0, z=R+1/500, and n=824 and 2266 at kappa=2/3 and 9/10 at the same offset, respectively; no finite cap is used for the theorem.
residual_risks: Only the exact scalar constant-step recurrence with its specified start is proved. Rational sample checks do not bound the first negative iterate uniformly and do not certify floating-point positivity.

originality.rationale: The distinct indexed November 2 positive-start phase diagram completely covers the fixed-start claim. Its A,B are the frozen B,C and its positive ratio w can be set to q=1/(1+z). Where the admissible set is w>=lambda_- this q qualifies by p(q)>0 and 2q>A; where only w=lambda_+ works it does not qualify, by the very same identities. The all-ratio and no-ratio branches are immediate. The resulting boundary is z_c for kappa<=1/2 and z_a above it, with the same degenerate endpoint and unique maximum. It is the full ratio classification, not the all-start radius alone, that gives this coverage. This is a coverage verdict against the current catalogue, not a claim about historical priority. The stronger record is dated later and explicitly refers to an earlier backward-Euler special result.
residual_risks: The November 2 record is later by calendar date and acknowledges an earlier BE analysis; this assessment does not deny or assign first priority. Full relevant text of Hundsdorfer–Ruuth–Spiteri was not readable, which does not affect demonstrated exact catalogue coverage.
